canonical_question: Does the use of a single linear regression for all three temperatures assume a constant activation energy (E_a) within the 850–1050 °C range?

question_variants.question: Does the use of a single linear regression for all three temperatures assume a constant activation energy (E_a) within the 850–1050 °C range?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The evidence states that the slope yields the value of -Ea/R in the temperature range of 850–1050 °C, which implies a calculation based on a single slope (linear regression) over that range. This method inherently assumes a constant activation energy (Ea) within that specific range for the calculation, as Ea is derived from the single slope value.

answers.answer: The use of a single slope calculation from -Ea/R in the range of 850–1050 °C assumes a constant activation energy (Ea) across this temperature interval to derive the single value reported.
answers.measurement_outcome: Activation energy calculated from single slope
answers.mechanism: Arrhenius relationship assumes constant Ea over the fitted range
answers.boundary_limitation: Assumption of constancy over the 850-1050 °C range is inherent to the single slope method described.
evidence_spans: A coarse grain microstructure having BCC/B2 phases was obtained in the as-cast HEA sample.
Only 5 min of straining of sample significantly refined the grain structure from 98 to 1 μm and 0.43 μm for the SFP_400 and SFP_1800 sample, respectively.
The ultrafine-grained samples showed a phase transition from BCC/B2 to FCC structure.
